program_name: Mechanical Engineering (Ingegneria Meccanica) - Second Cycle / Master's Degree [05861R]
teaching_language: Italian (primary language of instruction). The official corsi.unibs.it programme card states 'Language: Italian'. A minority of individual courses is delivered in English inside two of the five curricula (Biomechanics and, from A.Y. 2026/27, Energy Transition). No curriculum is delivered wholly in English, and the programme is NOT included in the University of Brescia's official list of 'Study programmes taught in English'.
campus: Brescia - Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (DIMI), University of Brescia. In-person programme.
english_delivery_scope: RESOLVED: Italian-medium programme with partial English-delivered modules in some curricula. None of the four enum values fits exactly; the programme is NOT 'fully_english' and NOT 'english_curriculum_within_italian_programme' in the strict sense used for e.g. the Management LM (whose 'International business' and 'Green economy and sustainability' curricula are wholly English-taught). Per-curriculum breakdown verified against the official CINECA course catalogue (unibs.coursecatalogue.cineca.it, the syllabus system linked as 'Syllabus' from unibs.it), 1st year A.Y. 2026/27 study plans (corso 1472): (1) AUTOMOTIVE VEHICLES (Autoveicoli, schemaCod=5) - 100% Italian; all 8 listed teachings tagged 'Italian' (Machine Design I, Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics and Convective Heat Transfer, Theory and Measurements of Mechanical Vibrations, Hydraulic and Thermal Fluid Machines, Propulsion Systems for Motor Vehicles and Numerical Fluid-Dynamics, Applied Economics in Engineering, Automatic Control, Laboratory of Vehicle Aerodynamics). (2) BIOMECHANICS (Biomeccanica, schemaCod=66) - MIXED, roughly one third English by credits: English-tagged courses are Biofluid Mechanics (3 CFU), Biomechanics (6 CFU), Sensors for Biosignals (6 CFU) and Production Technology for Biomechanics (3 CFU), i.e. approx. 18 CFU of approx. 51 CFU in year 1; the remainder (Machine Design I 9 CFU, Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics and Convective Heat Transfer 6 CFU, Mechatronics Systems Interacting with Humans 6 CFU, Applied Economics in Engineering 6 CFU, Ergonomics and Safety 6 CFU) is Italian. In year 2 (A.Y. 2025/26 plan) further English courses appear (Materials for Biomedical Applications 3 CFU; electives Light Alloys 6 CFU, Mechanobiology 3 CFU) alongside Italian core courses (Design of Biomechanical Structures, Hydraulic and Thermal Fluid Machines, Industrial Systems for Medical Device Manufacturing). (3) MECHANICAL DESIGN (Costruzioni, schemaCod=6) - 100% Italian; all 8 listed teachings tagged 'Italian'. (4) PRODUCTION (Produzione, schemaCod=8) - 100% Italian; all listed teachings tagged 'Italian'. (5) ENERGY TRANSITION (Transizione Energetica, schemaCod=9) - MIXED and newly shifting to English: in the 1st year A.Y. 2026/27 plan three courses are English-tagged (Turbomachinery and Wind Turbines 9 CFU, Energy Decarbonization 6 CFU, Chemistry and Thermodynamics for Energy Systems 6 CFU, approx. 21 CFU), while Machine Design I, Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics and Convective Heat Transfer, Systems Analysis and Optimization Lab, Applied Economics in Engineering and Sustainable Industrial Systems remain Italian; the equivalent courses in the A.Y. 2025/26 (2nd year) plan are all tagged Italian, so the English delivery in this curriculum is new from 2026/27. CONCLUSION: a student without Italian cannot complete this degree in any curriculum. The Biomechanics curriculum is the one the Italian programme description calls 'per la maggior parte in lingua inglese' / 'erogati in gran parte in lingua inglese', but that phrase refers only to the biomedical/specialisation subset of the curriculum's teachings, not to the whole curriculum.
programme_status: active_first_year - the programme is actively recruiting new students for A.Y. 2026/27. The official study-plan links publish a '1st year A.Y. 26-27' plan for all five curricula, and the Engineering LM admission page states the admission procedure for A.Y. 2026/27 was open 1 July - 30 September 2026. (For contrast, the sibling programme Digital Enterprise Technology Engineering is flagged on the same listing page as 'From the A.Y. 26/27, only the second year of the course will be active' - Mechanical Engineering carries no such phasing-out note.) [uncertain] Status for A.Y. 2027/28 is not yet published; the 2027/28 calls had not appeared as of 2026-09-06.
pre_evaluation_required: Yes, for candidates holding a foreign qualification. The University of Brescia runs a mandatory pre-evaluation (pre-assessment) of the foreign degree via the PICA online platform before admission to any Corso di laurea magistrale, explicitly covering 'master's degrees taught in Italian or English language'. A EUR 20 fee is charged for pre-assessment (and for pre-assessment plus LMINT scholarship applications). A.Y. 2026/27 rounds: (a) First round, reserved to non-EU candidates living abroad - deadline 15 March 2026 at noon Italian time; outcomes communicated end of May / beginning of June 2026. (b) Second round, reserved to EU and EU-equivalent citizens with a foreign degree (Law, Economics and Engineering areas) - open 16 July to 16 August 2026 at noon Italian time; outcomes by end of August 2026; only one application with one study programme allowed. Non-EU students living abroad who pass pre-assessment must then submit the formal study-visa application through the Universitaly portal. Candidates holding an Italian degree do not use PICA; they apply through the Esse3 personal account ('Pre-evaluation of Admission Requirements for Engineering Master's Programs'). Contact e-mail for admissions: internationalstudents@unibs.it. Platform: PICA. Source: https://www.unibs.it/en/international/degree-seeking-students/admission/pre-evaluation-masters-degrees
entry_test_name: None. There is no entry test (no TOLC, no SAT, no CISIA test) for this Master's degree. It is an 'unrestricted access' / 'free access' second-cycle programme: entry is governed by verification of curricular requirements plus verification of the adequacy of the candidate's personal preparation, decided by the CCSA of Industrial Engineering. The only test that may apply is the separate Italian-language proficiency test for non-EU candidates living abroad applying to Italian-taught programmes (TEST-ITALIANO-L2, CISIA), which is an admission-eligibility condition set by Ministry rules, not a selective entry exam for this degree. [uncertain] Whether the Italian-language test is enforced for this specific LM was not confirmed on a programme-specific page; the international admission pages state it generically as 'If Italian language proficiency is required, verify how to fulfill the condition'.
admission_type: open access (Italian: 'accesso libero'; the official programme card reads 'Type of admission: Free access course', and the Engineering LM admission page is titled 'Engineering (unrestricted access)'). Not a numerus clausus / restricted-access programme and not selection-by-ranking. Access is nevertheless conditional: the CCSA of Industrial Engineering verifies (1) curricular requirements and (2) adequacy of personal preparation, and the candidate is admitted only if both checks are positive. The decision of the CCSA is final ('con decisione insindacabile').
academic_requirements: Prerequisite qualification: a Laurea or three-year university diploma obtained in Italy, or another equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable. Curricular requirements: candidates must have acquired AT LEAST 108 CFU/ECTS across the following groups of Italian scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD), referenced to the Industrial Engineering bachelor class. (1) Basic training activities: (a) at least 25 CFU in 'Mathematics, computer science and statistics' (INF/01, ING-INF/05, MAT/02, MAT/03, MAT/05, MAT/06, MAT/07, MAT/08, MAT/09, SECS-S/02), of which at least 15 CFU in the group MAT/02, MAT/03, MAT/05; (b) at least 15 CFU in 'Physics and chemistry' (CHIM/03, CHIM/07, FIS/01, FIS/03). (2) Characterising training activities: at least 60 CFU in the sector group ICAR/08, ING-IND/08, ING-IND/09, ING-IND/10, ING-IND/11, ING-IND/12, ING-IND/13, ING-IND/14, ING-IND/15, ING-IND/16, ING-IND/17, ING-IND/21, ING-IND/22, ING-IND/35. In addition, at least FIVE of the following seven conditions must be met: (I) 6 CFU in ING-IND/08, /09, /10, /11; (II) 6 CFU in ING-IND/12; (III) 6 CFU in ING-IND/13; (IV) 6 CFU in ING-IND/14 or ICAR/08; (V) 6 CFU in ING-IND/15; (VI) 6 CFU in ING-IND/16; (VII) 6 CFU in ING-IND/21 or ING-IND/22. If a candidate lacks the curricular requirements, the CCSA specifies curricular integrations (credits or named courses) that must be obtained BEFORE a new admission application; integrations cannot be taken after admission. Personal preparation: adequacy is assessed per the programme's Regolamento Didattico, based on the previous university career and on the results obtained in the qualifying degree. The CCSA may assign admitted students individual study plans or impose prescriptions on the study plan. The programme totals 120 CFU over 2 years; the curriculum (one of five) is chosen at the moment of matriculation. Requirements are set by Art. 5 of the current academic regulations (Regolamento didattico) at https://www.unibs.it/it/regolamentomeclm, and the general procedure by the 'Regolamento per l'ammissione ai Corsi di laurea magistrale del CCSA Ingegneria Industriale' (https://www.unibs.it/sites/default/files/2021-05/Reg_amm_LM_DIMI_2017.pdf). Admission of non-Italian citizens holding a first-level degree not issued in Italy is additionally governed by MUR Prot. n. 7802 of 24 March 2014.
language_requirements: Formal requirement stated in the programme's admission rules: knowledge of a European Union language other than Italian at CEFR level B2 at minimum. Candidates holding only B1 CAN be admitted, but are assigned a study plan containing 3 CFU dedicated to acquiring further language knowledge. Verification methods for foreign-language knowledge are set in the programme's Regolamento Didattico. Attainment of B2 is also required to graduate. IMPORTANT PRACTICAL NOTE: this B2 requirement is a foreign-language (in practice English) requirement layered on top of Italian - it is NOT an alternative to Italian. Because the programme is delivered in Italian, Italian-language competence is the de facto operative requirement; non-EU candidates living abroad applying to Italian-taught programmes are directed to the Italian language test (TEST-ITALIANO-L2, CISIA) page. This programme does not appear in the university's 'Requirements for English taught postgraduate degrees 2026/27' document, so the B2-English-only admission route published there for Civil and Environmental Engineering, Management and Analytics and Data Science does NOT apply here. [uncertain] The exact Italian-language level required and the exemption conditions for this specific programme were not found on a programme-specific page.
application_deadline_eu: A.Y. 2026/27 (now closed as of 2026-09-06): admission procedure for Engineering Master's degrees open 1 July - 30 September 2026 via the Esse3 personal account; after that date, admission only on an exceptional basis via an Infostudente ticket request. EU / EU-equivalent citizens holding a FOREIGN degree additionally had to use the PICA pre-assessment second round, 16 July - 16 August 2026 at noon (Italian time), with outcomes by end of August 2026. [uncertain] A.Y. 2027/28 dates were not yet published as of 2026-09-06; the dates above are expected to recur on a similar calendar but must be re-verified.
application_deadline_non_eu: A.Y. 2026/27 (now closed as of 2026-09-06), separate from and earlier than the EU route: (1) PICA pre-assessment first round for non-EU candidates living abroad - deadline 15 March 2026 at noon (Italian time), which is also the round used to apply for the LMINT and STAR international scholarships; outcomes communicated between end of May and beginning of June 2026. (2) After a positive pre-assessment, the formal study-visa application had to be submitted through the Universitaly portal BY 31 AUGUST 2026 (this is the visa/pre-enrolment step and is distinct from the university admission deadline). (3) Enrolment is then completed online after eligibility is confirmed. Non-EU candidates already living in Italy follow a separate track ('Non-EU candidates living in Italy'). [uncertain] A.Y. 2027/28 dates not yet published as of 2026-09-06.
required_documents: For candidates with an Italian degree (via Esse3): if the degree is from the University of Brescia (completed or in progress), no documents are required; if from another Italian university, a self-certification of degree completion or of enrolment including the list of exams taken, plus an English language certificate if applicable. Graduates holding a degree issued under the regulations prior to D.M. 509/1999 must also upload the syllabi of the courses completed. For candidates with a FOREIGN qualification (via PICA pre-assessment, then enrolment): (1) the Diploma and the Transcript of Records in the original language, accompanied by an official translation into Italian or English unless already issued in one of those two languages; (2) the Diploma and Transcript legalised, or bearing the Apostille stamp, by the authorities of the relevant education system; (3) the Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore) issued by the competent Italian diplomatic representation. ALTERNATIVE to legalisation and Declaration of Value: for qualifications belonging to the systems listed in ARDI, the University accepts CIMEA statements issued via the Diplome online platform - the Statement of Verification (instead of legalised documents) and the Statement of Comparability (instead of the Declaration of Value). The University explicitly does NOT accept the ARDI Statement of Correspondence for enrolment-confirmation purposes. English language certificate where applicable (B2). A EUR 20 fee applies to the PICA pre-assessment application. Post-admission credit-recognition requests use the Esse3 path Student Office > Academic Record > Request for Credit Recognition, with self-certification of exams and syllabi. [uncertain] A programme-specific document checklist for Mechanical Engineering was not published; the above is the university-wide checklist that governs this programme.
entry_exam_or_test: No written or oral entry examination and no admission ranking. Admission is a documentary/administrative assessment: the CCSA of Industrial Engineering (which may appoint a dedicated Valutazione/Evaluation Commission) verifies (a) possession of the curricular requirements listed above, following an evaluation of the candidate's academic career, and (b) the adequacy of the candidate's personal preparation, assessed per the Regolamento Didattico on the basis of the previous university career and the results obtained in the qualifying degree. The candidate is admitted only if BOTH checks are positive; the decision is final. No interview is mentioned as a standard step for this programme, and no personal-preparation interview requirement was published on the programme pages. Processing after application: UNIBS graduates are confirmed within 7 working days; graduates from other Italian universities within 30 working days. Final-year UNIBS students with 30 credits or fewer remaining who meet the requirements may enrol and submit their study plan on the first Monday after their degree is awarded; final-year students at other Italian universities with only the thesis remaining may enrol after submitting a self-certification of degree completion via Infostudente. Foreign-qualification holders are instead assessed through the PICA pre-assessment procedure. [uncertain] Whether a personal-preparation interview is ever convened in practice is not stated on the public pages.

source_quotes.quote: The Second Cycle degree in Mechanical Engineering sets out the acquisition of 120 university credits. There are 5 curricula offered.

source_quotes.quote: Il Corso di Studio e articolato in cinque curricula, che consentono di sviluppare competenze piu specifiche in settori di particolare interesse dell'ingegneria meccanica: Curriculum Autoveicoli / Curriculum Biomeccanica / Curriculum Costruzioni / Curriculum Transizione Energetica / Curriculum Produzione
source_quotes.note: Italian names of the five curricula, embedded in the English page. 'Costruzioni' is rendered as 'Mechanical Design' in the English study-plan links.

source_quotes.quote: Curriculum Biomeccanica ... accanto ai tradizionali insegnamenti del percorso formativo in Ingegneria Meccanica, vengono impartite (per la maggior parte in lingua inglese) nozioni relative alla fluidodinamica dei sistemi biologici, alla schematizzazione e simulazione funzionale e strutturale di apparati e impianti, al comportamento dei materiali e biomateriali impiegati per applicazioni biomedicali, alle tecnologie di prototipazione e di fabbricazione di protesi e dispositivi, ai sensori per utilizzo biomedicale, nonche alle procedure per la gestione della qualita e sicurezza dei prodotti biomedicali.
source_quotes.note: THIS IS ONE HALF OF THE REPORTED CONFLICT. Translation: 'alongside the traditional teachings of the Mechanical Engineering programme, notions are delivered (for the most part in English) relating to biological fluid dynamics, ...'. Note the scope: the parenthetical 'per la maggior parte in lingua inglese' qualifies only the biomedical specialisation topics listed after it, NOT the whole curriculum, which also contains the Italian-taught traditional Mechanical Engineering core.

source_quotes.quote: la progettazione di sistemi e dispositivi per il settore biomedicale. A tale scopo, attraverso la frequenza di insegnamenti curriculari erogati in gran parte in lingua inglese, l'allievo integra la propria formazione mediante conoscenze e competenze relative alla fluidodinamica dei sistemi biologici, ...
source_quotes.note: Restatement in the learning-outcomes section: 'through attendance of curricular teachings delivered largely in English'. Again scoped to the biomedical-design strand only.

source_quotes.quote: All'acquisizione della conoscenza della terminologia disciplinare e della capacita di comunicare efficacemente in lingua inglese, contribuiscono sia la presenza di insegnamenti (curriculari e a scelta libera) erogati in lingua inglese, che l'uso di testi e materiale didattico in lingua inglese.
source_quotes.note: Confirms English is present as individual courses (curricular and elective) plus English textbooks/teaching material - i.e. an English component inside an Italian-medium degree, not English-medium delivery.

source_quotes.quote: Per accedere al Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Meccanica, i candidati devono avere acquisito, almeno 108 CFU nell'ambito dei seguenti gruppi di settori scientifico-disciplinari (SSD), con i limiti di volta in volta specificati.
source_quotes.note: Core curricular requirement: minimum 108 CFU across specified SSD groups.

source_quotes.quote: Per accedere al corso di Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Meccanica e richiesta inoltre la conoscenza di una lingua dell'Unione Europea oltre all'Italiano, almeno al livello B2 del CEFR. Gli studenti in possesso del livello di conoscenza B1 potranno accedere al corso di studio a fronte dell'assegnazione di un piano degli studi che prevede 3 CFU destinati all'acquisizione di ulteriori conoscenze linguistiche.
source_quotes.note: Language requirement: B2 in an EU language other than Italian; B1 admissible with a 3-CFU language add-on in the study plan.

source_quotes.quote: L'ammissione alla Laurea Magistrale sara deliberata con decisione insindacabile dal CCSA di Ingegneria Industriale sulla base della verifica del possesso dei requisiti curriculari, a seguito di una valutazione del curriculum accademico del candidato, e della verifica della preparazione personale. Il candidato sara ammesso solo in caso di esito positivo di entrambe le verifiche.
source_quotes.note: Admission mechanism: dual verification (curricular requirements + personal preparation), no entry exam.

uncertainty_notes:
ACCESS METHOD / VERIFICATION CAVEAT: unibs.it, corsi.unibs.it and unibs.coursecatalogue.cineca.it are all behind a Cloudflare-style 'Human Verification' managed challenge. Direct WebFetch returned HTTP 405 (corsi.unibs.it) and HTTP 403 (www.unibs.it and its PDF files); curl with a browser user-agent returned 405; loading the pages in an automated browser produced a 'Let's confirm you are human' interstitial that I did not bypass (completing bot-detection challenges is not permitted). All content above was therefore retrieved through a public text-extraction reader proxy (r.jina.ai) that fetched the official unibs.it / corsi.unibs.it / unibs.coursecatalogue.cineca.it URLs. The content is the official page content and every quote is attributed to its exact official URL, but the pages were NOT rendered and read directly in a first-party browser session, so a human should re-open the URLs to confirm before publication. Search-engine snippets were used only for initial discovery, not as a content source.

CONFLICT RESOLUTION - RESOLVED, with the exact conflicting statements: The research brief reported that the corsi.unibs.it listing showed this programme as 'English, open access' while the programme description said only the Biomechanics curriculum is 'mostly English'. Both current official listings contradict the 'English' half of that claim: (a) the programme card at https://corsi.unibs.it/en/mechanical-engineering states 'Language: Italian' and 'Type of admission: Free access course'; (b) the Engineering master's listing at https://corsi.unibs.it/en/masters-degree/engineering states 'Mechanical Engineering | Master's Degree | Where: Brescia | Language Italian | Type of admission: Free access course'. The 'open access' half of the claim IS correct. The most plausible source of the 'English' attribute is the official CINECA course catalogue, whose degree header at https://unibs.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2026/1472/... reads 'Two-year Master's degrees  English  Italian  Convenzionale' - a tag listing every language in which any course is delivered, which third-party aggregators can misread as 'the programme is in English'. Two independent official sources confirm the programme is NOT English-taught: it is absent from the university's complete list of 'Study programmes taught in English' (https://www.unibs.it/en/node/4464, updated 05/08/2026, five programmes only) and absent from the official 'Entry requirements for English taught Corsi di laurea magistrale' A.Y. 2026/27 PDF (three master's degrees only).

PER-CURRICULUM LANGUAGE - RESOLVED at course level, from the official CINECA syllabus 1st-year A.Y. 2026/27 study plans, which tag each course with its language: Automotive vehicles = 100% Italian; Mechanical Design (Costruzioni) = 100% Italian; Production = 100% Italian; Biomechanics = mixed, approx. 18 CFU English (Biofluid Mechanics, Biomechanics, Sensors for Biosignals, Production Technology for Biomechanics) of approx. 51 CFU; Energy Transition = mixed, approx. 21 CFU English (Turbomachinery and Wind Turbines, Energy Decarbonization, Chemistry and Thermodynamics for Energy Systems). NO curriculum is delivered entirely in English. Note the programme's own Italian prose description mentions English ONLY for Biomechanics and is now out of date: the Energy Transition curriculum acquired three English courses in A.Y. 2026/27 (the same courses were tagged Italian in the A.Y. 2025/26 plan) without the prose description being updated. This is a real internal inconsistency between the corsi.unibs.it narrative text and the CINECA syllabus, and it should be re-checked each academic year.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTIES: (1) Second-year A.Y. 2026/27 study plans are not yet published - only A.Y. 2025/26 second-year plans are linked, so the year-2 language mix for the 2026/27 intake may change (the Energy Transition shift shows this happens). (2) All application deadlines above are the A.Y. 2026/27 dates and had already passed as of the research date 2026-09-06; A.Y. 2027/28 calls were not yet published. (3) Whether the CISIA TEST-ITALIANO-L2 Italian-language test is enforced for this specific programme, and at what level, is stated only generically on the international admission pages, never on the programme's own pages. (4) No programme-specific document checklist exists; the document list given is the university-wide one. (5) The 'english_delivery_scope' enum in fields.yaml has no value that fits this case exactly - the programme is Italian-medium with partial English modules in two curricula, which is weaker than 'english_curriculum_within_italian_programme' (that value describes the Management LM, where two curricula are wholly English-taught). It is definitely not 'fully_english', not 'partial_third_year_english', and no longer 'conflicting_or_unverified' since the conflict has been resolved against English. (6) PRACTICAL RECOMMENDATION FOR ITALYPATH: this programme should NOT be listed as an English-taught option for international students - Italian is required to complete any of the five curricula.
